the Court made the following  O R D E R Heard the learned Additional Solicitor General for the petitioner.
The respondent was prosecuted for the offences punishable under Section 2(1)(a) and (j) read with Section 16(1)(a) as well as Section 7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The learned Magistrate passed an order of acquittal.
An application for leave to prefer appeal was filed before the Delhi Administration vs Vishwa Nath Khera.

1 High Court.
The High Court has declined to grant leave by passing the impugned order.
The first ground on which the order of acquittal was made was that the variation in the two test reports was more than the permissible limit of 3%.
Therefore, the benefit of doubt was granted to the respondent.
The second ground in the order of acquittal of the learned Magistrate was that the method adopted for analysis was not a sure test in the light of a decision of a High Court.
The learned Additional Solicitor General is right, insofar as the first ground is concerned.

This Court by a judgment dated 24th April, 2018 in Criminal Appeal No.625 of 2018 in the case of Delhi Administration v. Vidya Gupta took a view that there was no reason for the Court to even refer to the contents of report of the Public Analyst, as the law enjoins the Court to only consider the contents of the certificate of Director.
Therefore, to that extent, the view taken by the High Court is erroneous.
However, the order of the Trial Court is based on one more ground regarding the method/test used for analysis for detecting artificial colouring method.
Looking at the judgment of the High Court, we find that the said finding was either not assailed or was not considered by the High Court.
The allegation of commission of offence relates to 2002.
Hence, we are of the view that this is not a fit to exercise jurisdiction of this Court under Article 136 of the Constitution of India.
Subject to what is observed above, the Special Leave Petition is dismissed.
Pending application also stands disposed of.

(ANITA MALHOTRA) (RAVINDER KUMAR)
